subject: Civil Engineering
title: Concrete Cover and Crack Control
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Concrete Cover and Crack Control.

hook.text: Rebar too close to the surface rusts. Too deep and it can't resist tension. Cover matters.

buildup.text: Cover is the thickness of concrete between the rebar and the outside face — a protective shell.

discovery.text: Marine structures need 3 inches of cover. Interior slabs need only 0.75 inches.

twist.text: Cracks are inevitable, but keeping them narrow — under 0.3 mm — protects the steel inside.

climax.text: Spacing rebar closely distributes many small cracks instead of few large ones.

punchline.text: You can't prevent cracks. But you can make them too small to matter.

quiz.question: Why does marine concrete require more cover than interior concrete?
options: Marine concrete is exposed to higher loads from wave action
Saltwater penetrates concrete and corrodes rebar — more cover delays the attack
Marine concrete uses different types of aggregate that need more space

details.summary: Concrete cover is the minimum thickness of concrete between the reinforcement and the exposed surface, protecting rebar from corrosion by providing an alkaline barrier against moisture, chlorides, and carbon dioxide.
details.whyItMatters: Inadequate cover is the single most common cause of premature reinforcement corrosion. Maintaining specified cover thickness can extend a structure's life by decades.
takeaways: Cover thickness ranges from 25mm indoors to 75mm in marine environments
Cracks wider than 0.3mm allow accelerated chloride penetration to rebar
Spacers and chairs maintain proper cover distance during construction

faq.question: Why does concrete cover protect steel reinforcement from corrosion?
faq.answer: Fresh concrete is highly alkaline with pH around 12.5, which creates a passive oxide film on steel that prevents corrosion. Cover provides a physical barrier that slows penetration of chlorides and carbon dioxide that would destroy this passive protection.

faq.question: How do engineers control crack widths in concrete structures?
faq.answer: Engineers distribute reinforcement in more bars at closer spacing rather than fewer large bars. They limit reinforcement stress under service loads. They also specify maximum bar spacing and minimum reinforcement ratios.
